treatment_rationale.summary: Imatinib blocks certain kinase proteins, including KIT and platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha, that can drive susceptible gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) cells. The exact tumour mutation affects sensitivity; a KIT-positive label alone does not replace specialist molecular review. Normal tissues can also be affected. GIST is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/PDGFRA and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.

alternatives: Discuss current GIST-specific systemic options or trials, surgery in appropriate settings, surveillance where appropriate and symptom-focused supportive care.
limitations: The NCCP document describes up to three years after surgery. Later IMADGIST evidence supports disease-free survival benefit from extending treatment in selected high-risk patients, so three years should not be labelled universally optimal or imposed as an automatic stop. Advanced GIST requires its own evidence and continuation discussion.

endpoints.metric: Selected extension from three to six adjuvant years

treatment_rationale.summary: Sunitinib blocks several kinases, including KIT and blood-vessel growth receptors. After imatinib resistance or intolerance it may slow gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST) growth. Its effects on normal blood vessels and other tissues explain the need for blood-pressure, heart, thyroid and organ-function monitoring. GIST is a distinct tumour type. A specialist team reviews pathology, KIT/PDGFRA and other relevant molecular findings, prior treatment, symptoms and scans. Surgery may be appropriate for resectable disease or selected situations. Radiotherapy has a selective role, rather than being a routine partner to these tablets. Nutrition, symptom control and supportive or palliative care can be used alongside active cancer treatment.

treatment_rationale.line: Unresectable or metastatic GIST after imatinib resistance or intolerance

alternatives: Discuss current GIST-specific systemic options or trials, surgery in appropriate settings, surveillance where appropriate and symptom-focused supportive care.
limitations: The pivotal GIST trial used the 42-day schedule, not this 21-day schedule. Published pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modelling supports the rationale for two weeks on/one week off, but is not a randomised GIST noninferiority trial and does not establish identical outcomes.
